findings.text: Any caller in the deploy transaction can initialize the account again
onRedelegation reverts when the account has two or more interfaces
The account calls onUninstall twice on a pre-validation hook

withdrawDepositTo and the interface functions skip the hook: Code smells: `withdrawDepositTo`, `installInterface`, `installInterfaces` and `uninstallInterface` are `onlyEntryPointOrSelf` with no `withHook`, and the EntryPoint calls them directly from userOp call data — A userOp that calls `withdrawDepositTo` directly moves the EntryPoint deposit, and the inst

The multi-type decoder does not keep pointers inside initData: Code smells: the bounds checks use `calldatasize()` and not the end of `initData`; `add(baseOffset, calldataload(offset))` can wrap; `mul(types.length, 32)` can overflow — Pointers in `initData` can point outside the slice. We found no caller other than the owner who controls those pointers.

Any installed validator can approve a module install or a hook removal: Code smells: `_enableMode` and `_checkEmergencyUninstallSignature` take the validator from `signature[0:20]` and accept any installed validator — A limited validator, such as a session validator, can install a full-power validator. We did not confirm that a deployed validator signs these digests.

The fallback install accepts selector 0x00000000 against its own comment: Code smells: the comment bans `bytes4(0)` but the `require` does not check it; calldata of 1 to 4 zero bytes reaches that handler — The owner can install a handler for selector `0x00000000`. We found no path for an attacker who is not the owner.

The owner can install the same interface ID twice: Code smells: `installedIfaces.push` has no duplicate check; `_uninstallInterface` removes one copy and sets `supportedIfaces` to false — After two installs and one uninstall, the list keeps the ID while `supportsInterface` returns false. We found no party other than the owner who gains.

Multi-type install skips unknown module types and still reports success: Code smells: `_installModule` reverts on an unknown type, but `_multiTypeInstall` ignores types 0, 5, 6 and 7; `installModule` still emits `ModuleInstalled` — Off-chain tools record a module role that the account does not have. We found no loss of tokens.

One reverting validator makes ERC-7739 detection revert: Code smells: `_get7739Version` calls `isValidSignatureWithSender` on each validator without `try` — One installed validator that reverts on an empty signature makes the detection call revert for every caller. We did not confirm an integrator that depends on this detection.

An old emergency timelock survives an uninstall and a reinstall of the hook: Code smells: `emergencyUninstallTimelock` uses the hook address as its key and not the hook type; only the removal branch clears it; the signed struct has no phase and no deadline, so the submitter picks start or remove — A signer can remove a reinstalled hook with no new one-day wait, because the o

The hook runs twice for one user operation: Code smells: `executeUserOp` has `withHook` and delegatecalls `address(this)`; the inner `execute` also has `withHook` — A hook that counts spend per call counts one operation twice. We did not test a real hook module.

The initializer checks 24 bytes but reads a 64-byte header: Code smells: the check is `initData.length >= 24`; the code does not check the bootstrap offset or `bootstrapCall.length`; `bootstrap` keeps dirty upper bits — The initializer reads the bootstrap offset and length with no bounds check. Only the factory or the account calls it, so we found no outside

isValidSignature reverts instead of returning the ERC-1271 failure value: Code smells: `_handleValidator` reverts for a validator that is not installed; `signature[0:20]` reverts for a signature shorter than 20 bytes — The function reverts for a bad signature prefix instead of returning `0xffffffff`. We did not find a caller that breaks on the revert.

onRedelegation leaves module state and account storage in place: Code smells: `popAll` clears the lists but calls no `onUninstall`; the `_DEFAULT_VALIDATOR` owner data, `emergencyUninstallTimelock` and `nonces` stay set — After the EOA redelegates and later delegates back, the old default-validator owner can sign again. uninstallModule accepts the zero address as an installed module: Code smells: `_isModuleInstalled` returns true for `address(0)` on an empty hook slot, an empty pre-validation slot or a selector with no fallback handler — The account emits `ModuleUninstalled` for a module that was never installed, so an indexer records a wrong state. We found no loss of tokens.
